result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend B, explain that multiple choice tests recognizing a good answer rather than giving one, run the 15-hour math correctly, and add a short auto-scored quiz to give the VP some scale. B's plan holds together better: two peer rounds, then one lead round, cuts the lead's time to about 5 hours, and it includes a fallback if even that is too much. A cuts the lead's time further, to about 75 minutes, but says everything fits in 2 hours when the demo plus three role-plays already takes about 105 minutes before prep, and its description of the peer rotation is muddled. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend B, explain that picking from options is different from giving an answer out loud, and add a short quiz to give the VP something that scales. A's math holds up: one lead round per rep is 15 × 20 minutes, or about 5 hours, and it gives a fallback if even that isn't possible. B says the lead can join one 20-minute round per rep, yet puts the cost at about 5 minutes per rep (75 minutes in total), which doesn't add up, and its description of how the peer role-plays rotate is muddled.
